newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Jinro default news seen depressing Seoul stocks.
newsitem.headline: Jinro default news seen depressing Seoul stocks.

text.p: News that Jinro Ltd had defaulted on loan repayments last night was expected to dampen the market again, which had already been suffering from the Kia crisis, brokers said on Tuesday.
Jinro Ltd, South Korea's largest distiller, defaulted on repayments of promissory notes worth about eight billion won, said Jinro's main creditor Commercial Bank of Korea.
The composite stock index ended 1.60 points higher at 733.92 on Monday.
"The Jinro news could be another blow to the market," said Choo Hee-yup of Dongwon Securities.
Brokers said news of a decision by Kia's unions that they would not honour a no-dispute agreement with management would also erode the market sentiment.
"Creditor banks want Kia to come up with a more intensive restructuring plan. But Kia is now caught up in the middle of its unions and creditor banks," said Choo.
Brokers said falling customer deposits with brokerage houses were also bad news for the market.
